category: Nouns that end in -s but are singular

examples: The news is better than we expected.
Have you heard the news?
That's the best piece of news all week.
No news is good news.
He watches the news every night at six.
It was on the news this morning.
Three news organizations reported the same figure.

senses.head: Information about events
examples: The news is better than we expected.
Have you heard the news?
That's the best piece of news all week.
No news is good news.

senses.head: Broadcast news
examples: He watches the news every night at six.
It was on the news this morning.

senses.head: Attributive
examples: Three news organizations reported the same figure.

entries.agreement: singular verb — the news is good
entries.counted with: a piece of news, an item of news, a news story
entries.contrast: ✗ The news are good is wrong, and ✗ a news is wrong. This trips up speakers of most European languages, where the equivalent word is plural. For one item say a piece of news or a news story.

entries.meaning: The study of numbers, quantity, and space.
examples: Mathematics is required for the degree.
She teaches mathematics at the high school.
Pure mathematics interests him more than applied.
Math was never my strong subject.
The mathematics behind the model is straightforward.

senses.head: The academic field
examples: Mathematics is required for the degree.
She teaches mathematics at the high school.
Pure mathematics interests him more than applied.
Math was never my strong subject.
The mathematics behind the model is straightforward.

entries.counted with: a branch of mathematics, a field of mathematics
entries.variants: shortened to math in American English, maths in British
entries.contrast: ✗ Mathematics are difficult is wrong. Note the American short form is math — singular, no -s — while British English says maths. Both take a singular verb.

entries.meaning: The science of matter, energy, and their interactions.
examples: Physics is his favorite subject.
She studied physics at Berkeley.
Particle physics requires enormous machines.
The physics of flight is well understood.
Physics explains why the bridge failed.

senses.head: The academic field
examples: Physics is his favorite subject.
She studied physics at Berkeley.
Particle physics requires enormous machines.
The physics of flight is well understood.
Physics explains why the bridge failed.

entries.contrast: ✗ Physics are hard is wrong. Unlike politics and statistics, this word has no plural sense at all — it is always singular.

entries.meaning: The study of production and consumption; also the financial aspects of something.
examples: Economics is required for the business degree.
He teaches economics at a small college.
Behavioral economics has changed the field.
The economics of the project are terrible.
The economics of rural hospitals have never worked.

senses.head: The academic field
examples: Economics is required for the business degree.
He teaches economics at a small college.
Behavioral economics has changed the field.

senses.head: The financial realities of something
examples: The economics of the project are terrible.
The economics of rural hospitals have never worked.

entries.countability: singular as a field; plural in the 'financial aspects' sense
entries.agreement: singular as a field — economics is a social science; plural for aspects — the economics of the deal are poor
entries.contrast: The split is real and useful. Economics is a difficult subject — the field. The economics of solar power are improving — the financial facts of a particular case. Both are correct in their own sense.

entries.meaning: Political activity; also a person's political opinions.
examples: Politics is not for the thin-skinned.
She went into politics after law school.
Office politics makes the job harder than the work does.
His politics are hard to pin down.
Their politics have shifted over the years.

senses.head: Political activity or the field
examples: Politics is not for the thin-skinned.
She went into politics after law school.
Office politics makes the job harder than the work does.

senses.head: Someone's political views
examples: His politics are hard to pin down.
Their politics have shifted over the years.

entries.countability: singular as a field; plural as someone's opinions
entries.agreement: singular as a field — politics is a dirty business; plural for views — her politics are complicated
entries.contrast: The commonest error is applying one verb to both senses. Politics is exhausting refers to the activity; his politics are well to the left refers to his opinions. Both are standard.

entries.meaning: The science of collecting and analyzing numerical data; also the data itself.
examples: Statistics is required for the psychology major.
She teaches statistics to first-year students.
The statistics are disputed by both sides.
These statistics come from the census.
Crime statistics have fallen for six years.
That's a startling statistic.

senses.head: The academic field
examples: Statistics is required for the psychology major.
She teaches statistics to first-year students.

senses.head: Numerical data
examples: The statistics are disputed by both sides.
These statistics come from the census.
Crime statistics have fallen for six years.

senses.head: One figure
examples: That's a startling statistic.

entries.countability: singular as a field; plural as data
entries.agreement: singular as a field — statistics is a branch of mathematics; plural for figures — the statistics are disputed
entries.contrast: This one has a true countable singular: a statistic means one number. So statistics is hard is the subject, these statistics are wrong are the numbers, and that's a depressing statistic is one of them. All three are correct.

entries.meaning: The study of moral principles; also someone's moral standards.
examples: Ethics is required for all medical students.
Medical ethics has changed enormously.
His ethics are questionable at best.
Their business ethics were never in doubt.
Journalistic ethics require naming the source.

senses.head: The philosophical field
examples: Ethics is required for all medical students.
Medical ethics has changed enormously.

senses.head: Moral principles held by someone
examples: His ethics are questionable at best.
Their business ethics were never in doubt.
Journalistic ethics require naming the source.

entries.countability: singular as a field; plural as principles
entries.agreement: singular as a field — ethics is a branch of philosophy; plural for principles — his ethics are questionable
entries.counted with: a branch of ethics, a code of ethics
entries.contrast: Same split as politics. The discipline is singular; a person's moral standards are plural.

entries.meaning: The sport of physical exercises; figuratively, elaborate contortions.
examples: Gymnastics is one of the hardest sports on the body.
She did gymnastics until she was sixteen.
Olympic gymnastics draws huge audiences.
The mental gymnastics required were exhausting.
His verbal gymnastics fooled nobody.

senses.head: The sport
examples: Gymnastics is one of the hardest sports on the body.
She did gymnastics until she was sixteen.
Olympic gymnastics draws huge audiences.

senses.head: Elaborate contortions
examples: The mental gymnastics required were exhausting.
His verbal gymnastics fooled nobody.

entries.countability: singular as a sport; plural as feats
entries.agreement: singular for the sport — gymnastics is demanding; plural for feats — his verbal gymnastics were impressive
entries.contrast: The literal sport is singular. The figurative sense — elaborate contortions of logic or language — is plural: mental gymnastics are required to believe that.

entries.meaning: Organized sports; in British usage, track and field.
examples: Athletics is heavily funded at that school.
He works in the athletics department.
College athletics generates enormous revenue.
She competed in athletics at the national level.
The athletics events begin on Tuesday.

senses.head: Organized sports
examples: Athletics is heavily funded at that school.
He works in the athletics department.
College athletics generates enormous revenue.

senses.head: Track and field
examples: She competed in athletics at the national level.
The athletics events begin on Tuesday.

entries.countability: singular, and plural in the 'sports programs' sense
entries.agreement: usually singular — athletics is well funded here
entries.variants: in American English athletics means organized sports generally; in British English it means track and field
entries.contrast: The transatlantic difference matters. An American university's athletics department runs all its sports; a British athletics meeting is running, jumping, and throwing.

examples: Measles is highly contagious.
He had measles as a child.
Measles was nearly eliminated in the 1990s.
Twelve cases of measles were reported.
The measles vaccine is given in two doses.

senses.head: The disease
examples: Measles is highly contagious.
He had measles as a child.
Measles was nearly eliminated in the 1990s.
Twelve cases of measles were reported.
The measles vaccine is given in two doses.

entries.agreement: singular verb — measles is highly contagious
entries.contrast: ✗ Measles are contagious is wrong. All the -s disease names behave this way: mumps, rabies, diabetes, shingles, herpes. To count outbreaks, say cases of measles.

entries.meaning: The contagious viral disease causing swollen glands.
examples: Mumps is rare now because of vaccination.
She caught mumps from her brother.
Mumps causes painful swelling of the jaw.
Two cases of mumps appeared on campus.
He was out of school for a month with the mumps.

senses.head: The disease
examples: Mumps is rare now because of vaccination.
She caught mumps from her brother.
Mumps causes painful swelling of the jaw.
Two cases of mumps appeared on campus.
He was out of school for a month with the mumps.

entries.agreement: singular verb — mumps is rare now
entries.contrast: ✗ Mumps are is wrong. Often used with the: he has the mumps.

entries.meaning: The viral disease transmitted by animal bite.
examples: Rabies is almost always fatal once symptoms appear.
The dog was vaccinated against rabies.
Rabies is carried by bats and raccoons here.
Three cases of rabies were confirmed in the county.
He needed the rabies shots after the bite.

senses.head: The disease
examples: Rabies is almost always fatal once symptoms appear.
The dog was vaccinated against rabies.
Rabies is carried by bats and raccoons here.
Three cases of rabies were confirmed in the county.
He needed the rabies shots after the bite.

entries.agreement: singular verb — rabies is almost always fatal
entries.contrast: ✗ Rabies are is wrong. The word is from Latin rabies, 'madness', where the -es was never a plural.

entries.meaning: The metabolic disease affecting blood sugar.
examples: Diabetes is manageable with the right treatment.
Type 2 diabetes is far more common.
His diabetes was diagnosed at forty.
Diabetes runs in her family.
Untreated diabetes damages the kidneys.

senses.head: The disease
examples: Diabetes is manageable with the right treatment.
Type 2 diabetes is far more common.
His diabetes was diagnosed at forty.
Diabetes runs in her family.
Untreated diabetes damages the kidneys.

entries.counted with: a case of diabetes, a type of diabetes
entries.contrast: ✗ Diabetes are is wrong. Both final-syllable pronunciations — -teez and -tis — are accepted in American English.

examples: Billiards is played on a table without pockets.
He learned billiards from his grandfather.
Billiards was once the more fashionable game.
They played billiards until midnight.
A game of billiards takes real patience.

senses.head: The game
examples: Billiards is played on a table without pockets.
He learned billiards from his grandfather.
Billiards was once the more fashionable game.
They played billiards until midnight.
A game of billiards takes real patience.

entries.agreement: singular verb — billiards is played on a smaller table
entries.contrast: ✗ Billiards are is wrong when naming the game. All game names in -s work this way: darts is, checkers is, dominoes is, cards is. The equipment, however, is plural: the darts are missing.

entries.meaning: The game of throwing small pointed missiles at a board; also the missiles.
examples: Darts is more popular in Britain than here.
They play darts every Thursday.
Darts requires far more skill than people assume.
His darts are custom-weighted.
Three darts were stuck in the wall.

senses.head: The game
examples: Darts is more popular in Britain than here.
They play darts every Thursday.
Darts requires far more skill than people assume.

senses.head: The objects
examples: His darts are custom-weighted.
Three darts were stuck in the wall.

entries.countability: singular as a game; plural as the objects
entries.agreement: singular for the game — darts is popular in bars; plural for the objects — the darts are in the case
entries.counted with: a game of darts; one object is a dart
entries.contrast: The clearest example of the game/equipment split. Darts is harder than it looks — the game. His darts are custom-made — the objects.

entries.meaning: The board game played with flat round pieces.
examples: Checkers is easy to learn and hard to master.
They played checkers on the porch all summer.
Checkers was solved by computer in 2007.
Half the checkers are missing from the box.
The red checkers were made of plastic.

senses.head: The game
examples: Checkers is easy to learn and hard to master.
They played checkers on the porch all summer.
Checkers was solved by computer in 2007.

senses.head: The pieces
examples: Half the checkers are missing from the box.
The red checkers were made of plastic.

entries.countability: singular as a game; plural as the pieces
entries.agreement: singular for the game — checkers is simple to learn; plural for pieces — the checkers are missing
entries.variants: the British name for the same game is draughts, pronounced drafts
entries.contrast: Same split as darts: the game is singular, the pieces are plural.
